step1_figure.circuit_type: MOSFET differential pair with diode-connected load (M3) and triode-biased load (M4)
step1_figure.description: A source-coupled NMOS differential pair (M1, M2) biased by a 40 uA tail current sink, loaded on one side by a diode-connected PMOS (M3) and on the other side by a grounded-gate PMOS operating in the triode region (M4).

dc_branch_current.description: DC drain current flowing through each half of the balanced differential pair

equation.explanation: Due to circuit symmetry with equal gate bias on M1 and M2, the tail current splits evenly between both branches.
equation.assumptions: M1 and M2 are identical and saturated.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined purely by tail current bias Ibias = 40 uA.

vgs_input_pair.description: Gate-to-source DC operating voltage of NMOS input transistors M1 and M2

equation.formula: VGS = sqrt(2 * ID / (KPn * W / L)) + VTHN
equation.explanation: Square-law saturation characteristic relating drain current to gate-source overdrive.
equation.assumptions: Square-law model, saturation, no channel-length modulation.

sky130_expected.calculation: For W/L = 10u / 1u = 10, ID = 20 uA, KPn = 270 uA/V^2, Vthn0 = 0.42 V: Vov = sqrt(2 * 20u / (270u * 10)) = 0.122 V. VGS = 0.42 + 0.122 = 0.542 V (without body effect; with body effect Vth ~ 0.5-0.6V, VGS ~ 0.65-0.75V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Body effect on vs12 increases effective Vth above VTHN0.

dc_source_voltage_vs12.description: Common source node DC potential of M1 and M2

source.reference: Ex. 9.5 and simulation output on page 283

equation.explanation: The source potential sits one VGS below the DC input gate bias.

sky130_expected.calculation: VS12 = 0.9 V - VGS1. For typical VGS1 ≈ 0.68 V, VS12 ≈ 0.22 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Tail node voltage must allow tail current source to stay in compliance.

vsg_m3.description: Source-to-gate DC operating voltage of diode-connected PMOS M3

equation.explanation: Diode-connected PMOS carries ID = 20 uA in saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: M3 body is tied to VDD so there is no body effect on M3.

dc_vd13.description: DC drain potential of M1 and M3

equation.explanation: Since M3 is diode-connected to VDD, the drain potential is VDD minus VSG3.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Node vd13 sits approximately 0.6 V below VDD.

dc_vd24.description: DC drain potential of M2 and M4

equation.formula: VD24 = VDD - VSD4 ≈ VDD - ID * Rch_M4
equation.explanation: M4 has gate tied to 0V (VSG = VDD = 1.8V), driving it deep into the triode region where VSD is very small.
equation.assumptions: M4 operates as a linear resistor in deep triode.

sky130_expected.reasoning: M4 acts as a low resistance pull-up to VDD.

rch_m4.description: Channel resistance of triode-biased PMOS M4

equation.explanation: MOSFET channel resistance in the deep triode region.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by PMOS triode transconductance parameter and gate overdrive.

gm_nmos.description: Transconductance of input NMOS pair M1 and M2

equation.explanation: Small-signal transconductance of NMOS in saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical transconductance for 20 uA bias in 10/1 NMOS.

gm_pmos_m3.description: Transconductance of diode-connected load PMOS M3

sky130_expected.reasoning: Load impedance at vd13 is 1/gm3 ≈ 4.08 kΩ.

ac_gain_vd13.description: Small-signal AC voltage gain from single-ended input vg1 to output vd13

equation.explanation: Input signal splits equally across differential pair (vgs1 = vin/2), producing AC current id1 = gm1 * vin / 2. This current flows into diode load resistance 1/gm3.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Ratio of input NMOS gm to load PMOS gm divided by 2 due to single-ended input drive.

ac_gain_vd24.description: Small-signal AC voltage gain from single-ended input vg1 to output vd24

equation.explanation: AC current id2 = -gm1 * vin / 2 flows into channel resistance Rch_M4, producing an attenuated output.
equation.assumptions: M4 in deep triode acts as a linear resistor Rch_M4.

sky130_expected.calculation: Av24 = (328.6 uA/V * 483 ohm) / 2 = 0.0794 V/V (-22.0 dB). For 1 mV AC input, vd24_ac = 79.4 uV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Very low gain because M4 triode resistance is only a few hundred ohms.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench verifying DC bias points (branch currents, node voltages, triode resistance) and AC small-signal gains for Example 9.5 on SKY130.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Baker CMOS Chapter 9 - Example 9.5 Differential Circuit
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=10u L_xm1=1u
.param W_xm2=10u L_xm2=1u
.param W_xm3=30u L_xm3=1u
.param W_xm4=30u L_xm4=1u

* Circuit Netlist (DUT)
xm2 vd24 N001 vs12 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
VDD VDD 0 1.8
Ibias vs12 0 40u
xm1 vd13 vg1 vs12 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
xm4 vd24 0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
xm3 vd13 vd13 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
VG1 vg1 0 DC 0.9 AC 1m SIN(0.9 1m 10k)
VG2 N001 0 0.9

* Zero-volt sources to accurately measure drain currents
* (as discussed in Fig. 9.9)

.control
save all

* 1. Operating Point Analysis
op

let v_vs12 = v(vs12)
let v_vd13 = v(vd13)
let v_vd24 = v(vd24)
let v_vgs1 = v(vg1) - v(vs12)
let v_vsg3 = v(vdd) - v(vd13)
let v_vsd4 = v(vdd) - v(vd24)

* Drain current in M4 is half tail current = 20uA
let rch_m4_calc = v_vsd4 / 20e-6

print v_vs12 v_vd13 v_vd24 v_vgs1 v_vsg3 v_vsd4 rch_m4_calc

* 2. AC Analysis
ac dec 100 1 10k

let gain_vd13 = v(vd13) / 1m
let gain_vd24 = v(vd24) / 1m
let gain_vd13_db = vdb(vd13) + 60
let gain_vd24_db = vdb(vd24) + 60

meas ac av_vd13_lf find gain_vd13 at=1k
meas ac av_vd24_lf find gain_vd24 at=1k
meas ac av_vd13_mag find v(vd13) at=1k
meas ac av_vd24_mag find v(vd24) at=1k

* 3. Transient Analysis (from Baker's LTspice settings)
tran 1u 300u
meas tran vd13_pk2pk pp v(vd13)
meas tran vd24_pk2pk pp v(vd24)

quit
.endc
.end
